verdict.root_cause: Frontend's shipping-quote gRPC calls are dialed at 172.18.0.7:50050 and refused at the TCP connect step — name resolution succeeds, but nothing accepts on that port [tr_bf4e2b4d888f]. All frontend errors surface through the gRPC client stack as propagated remote statuses (13 INTERNAL wrapping transport Unavailable, later bare 14 UNAVAILABLE), not from frontend's own logic [tr_bf4e2b4d888f]. Meanwhile checkoutservice completes end-to-end orders through the final minute [tr_f965864a3e76] and cartservice serves normally [tr_11494c4f1ae3], so the wider order path is not broken. Only frontend's leg fails, and only partially — error ratio roughly doubled to a ~12.8% peak [tr_054d0c4b99b1]. The most consistent reading is that the shipping-quote endpoint address frontend uses names the wrong port/target: the wrong value is itself what breaks the request.
verdict.reasoning: The log evidence pins the failure to the TCP connect step on frontend's outbound hop, excluding DNS, TLS/authz, ingress 5xx, frontend application code, and a slow-but-serving backend (no DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) [tr_bf4e2b4d888f]. That leaves 'nothing listening where frontend dials.' The discriminator between a dead shipping backend and a misaddressed client is checkoutservice, which is a single long-lived process placing orders successfully at both window edges [tr_f965864a3e76] — hard to reconcile with the shipping dependency being wholly down. The partial, non-total error ratio [tr_054d0c4b99b1] fits one misaddressed dependency path rather than a service-wide outage. Both change queries ran forward from onset and cannot see a pre-incident edit [tr_44b207d6043c, tr_a25b9fc77192], so the change record neither supports nor refutes this.
open_questions: No change query covered the hours before 20:38:15, so the actual edit that set the endpoint/port was never observed.
The shipping-quote service was never dispatched on directly — its process state, listening port, and whether checkoutservice reaches it on a different address are unverified.
cartservice metrics returned no samples in either window [tr_4262b1cb6929], leaving an instrumentation gap; frontend metrics have no per-route or per-dependency breakdown [tr_054d0c4b99b1].

alternatives.root_cause: The shipping-quote service itself is down or crash-looping, and frontend's refused connects are the symptom of an absent listener.
alternatives.why_not: checkoutservice completes full order flows including downstream writes through the window's end [tr_f965864a3e76], which a wholly unreachable shipping dependency should have disrupted; and the shipping service was never directly inspected either way.

alternatives.root_cause: The shipping-quote service was redeployed on a changed listening port, leaving frontend's unchanged address pointing at a dead port.
alternatives.why_not: The one-hop change query around checkoutservice recorded no port or dependency change [tr_a25b9fc77192], though its window began at onset and could not see a pre-onset rollout.

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change in any series is expected. Frontend's error ratio should continue at roughly its incident-window level (mean ~0.032, peaks ~12.8%) and the gRPC client log lines naming `dial tcp 172.18.0.7:50050: connect: connection refused` / bare 14 UNAVAILABLE should keep appearing until someone acts on the real listener. That continuation is itself the observable: it confirms nothing was disturbed by this step.
proposal.if_wrong: Three things would show abstention was the wrong call. (1) A change-history query widened to cover the hours *before* 2026-09-07T20:38:15 returns a frontend config or endpoint edit with a recorded prior value — that would satisfy revert_config's preconditions and make a config revert on frontend the right proposal. (2) A direct dispatch on the shipping-quote service shows a healthy process listening on a port other than 50050, pinning the fault to frontend's address value rather than to a dead backend. (3) The error ratio climbs well past ~12.8% toward total failure, which would raise the cost of waiting above the cost of acting on a medium-confidence diagnosis. Absent any of these, waiting is cheap: 87% of frontend calls still succeed [tr_054d0c4b99b1] and checkoutservice completes orders end-to-end through the final minute [tr_f965864a3e76].
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is duration: the shipping-quote leg stays broken and users keep hitting a partial checkout failure for as long as it takes a human to run the pre-window change query or dispatch on the shipping-quote host. That is a real cost, not zero. It is accepted here because every permitted action carries a larger one. revert_config is the class the synthesizer named, but its preconditions are explicitly unmet: the change-history query for frontend returned no changes of any kind [tr_44b207d6043c], so there is no recorded prior configuration to restore and no in-window config change named by evidence — the same result also notes the queried window never covered the hours before 20:38:15, so the edit that set the endpoint was never observed. Reverting to an unrecorded prior state is not a revert, it is a guess. restart_service is worse: the evidence points at a wrong address value, not at process state, and recreating frontend discards cache, resets connections for every live user session, and cannot change the endpoint the container is configured with. rollback_image has no deploy or image change in evidence to roll back to. scale_service is unavailable per ADR-0029. Most importantly, the service that actually is not listening on 172.18.0.7:50050 was never dispatched on and is not in the blast radius, so the system cannot legally touch the thing the mechanism implicates.
proposal.blast_radius: None. No service is modified, so no caller of frontend, checkoutservice, cartservice, productcatalogservice, adservice, or recommendationservice sees anything change. The existing blast radius persists unchanged: frontend users on the shipping-quote path continue to see errors at ~12.8% peak; loadgenerator continues to record them; the wider order path via checkoutservice and cartservice remains unaffected [tr_f965864a3e76, tr_11494c4f1ae3]. Note that two blind spots survive this abstention and should be closed before any later action: cartservice has no metric series in either window [tr_4262b1cb6929] and frontend metrics carry no per-route or per-dependency breakdown [tr_054d0c4b99b1], so post-action confirmation on the shipping-quote leg specifically would have to come from logs, not metrics.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alert on frontend followed immediately by the load generator indicates user-facing impact, not a lone warning. No open incidents to attribute it to, and any of frontend's five direct dependencies could be the source, so evidence is needed.
